JNJ.rationale: JNJ is a high-quality healthcare franchise with durable competitive positions in multiple myeloma and MedTech, strong balance sheet (interest coverage 25x, cash $22B), and ~$20B annual FCF supporting 64 consecutive dividend increases. However, the stock is fundamentally unattractive at current levels on all three pillars. Pillar 1 (fundamentals/trajectory): Margins are compressing — net margin fell from 27.3% to 21.8%, gross margin dropped 3.3pp QoQ to 66.3%, ROE declined from 31.7% to 25.9%. Q4 operating cash flow collapsed to $2.51B (QoQ -72.6%). TTM net income of $26.92B is inflated by a Q1 2025 anomaly (operating income $13.63B vs ~$5-7.5B in normal quarters); normalized annual earnings are ~$21B. Revenue growth is low-single-digit (+0.3% QoQ). Pillar 2 (valuation): P/E of 30.1x sits at the absolute top of the 365-day range (17.2-31.1x), representing ~72% PE expansion in twelve months on declining margins — pure multiple expansion, not fundamental improvement. Earnings yield of 3.3% is below the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.54%. P/B of 7.8x is at the top of its range. On normalized EPS of ~$8.50-9.00, the clean P/E is 29-30x for a low-single-digit grower. If PE mean-reverts to 22-24x on normalized earnings, implied price is $187-216, 17-28% below current $259.10. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): Q2 earnings on July 15 could be a negative catalyst — options imply only 4.3% move, consensus EPS $2.85, but the Q1 2025 anomaly will roll off TTM comps, potentially exposing the true earnings run-rate to investors anchoring on inflated trailing figures. FTC antitrust overhang on Stelara and ongoing talc litigation ($32M recent verdict) add downside risk. The stock is near its 52-week high ($259.10 vs $269.43) with no fundamental justification for the rerating.
